subject: european hamster
title: Feed These Hamsters Only Corn and the Mothers Eat Their Pups

scenes.text: Scientists changed one thing, and hamster mothers ate their pups.
It happened in a lab in France, with wild European hamsters. Half got wheat. Half got corn.
Wheat-fed mothers raised about four out of five pups. Corn-fed mothers raised five percent.
They stashed newborns with their corn hoard, then ate them.
The cause: corn lacks usable vitamin B3. Add the vitamin back, and the mothers behaved normally again.
In the wild, these hamsters live in endless cornfields. That may be one reason they're disappearing.

description:
When wild-caught European hamsters were fed a corn-based diet in the lab, the mothers ate almost all of their pups.
In the study, led by Mathilde Tissier at the University of Strasbourg and published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B in 2017, wheat-fed mothers weaned about four-fifths of their pups and corn-fed mothers only 5 percent. The cause was a lack of vitamin B3, the same deficiency behind pellagra in people; adding the vitamin to the corn diet stopped the behaviour. In Alsace the endangered hamsters live among maize monocultures.
Did you know a single missing vitamin could do this? Comment below.
first_comment: The same deficiency, pellagra, killed about three million people who lived mostly on corn. Which everyday food hides the strangest danger?
